title: SYSK Selects: What is a hangover, really?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun (originally aired October 29) on hangovers: the hosts open with banter about past drinking experiences, then explain the medical term "veisalgia," the diuretic effect of vasopressin suppression and dehydration, loss of electrolytes and glycogen, glutamine and sleep disruption, the role of congeners and darker liquors, acetaldehyde metabolism with glutathione and cysteine, why women and people around age 24 may suffer more, beer carbonation and drinking order, vomiting, and a range of hangover cures (hair of the dog, coffee, fatty food, bananas, eggs, fruit juice, aspirin, over-the-counter hangover pills, water pacing). The episode closes with Kiva promotion and a listener email from Mark, a former 2000 Census enumerator in Fishkill, New York, about his experiences going door to door.

segments.title: Opening banter and hangover experiences
segments.summary: Chuck introduces his pick and the hosts joke about drinking, under-21 listeners, and their personal hangover experiences and symptoms.

segments.title: Name and origin of hangover
segments.summary: The medical term veisalgia is introduced, described as from a Norwegian word for unease after debauchery and a Greek word for pain, along with a Bible verse from Isaiah 5:11 about rising early to drink.

segments.title: Vasopressin, diuresis and dehydration
segments.summary: Alcohol suppresses vasopressin so the kidneys send excess water to the bladder, causing frequent urination, dehydration and brain shrinkage that pulls on the meninges and causes headache. A side anecdote about drink-till-you-pee promotions.

segments.title: Electrolytes, glycogen and glutamine
segments.summary: Urination also removes electrolytes such as salt, potassium and magnesium, and glycogen is depleted, contributing to weakness and fatigue. Alcohol blocks glutamine production, and the body overproduces it after drinking, disrupting sleep.

segments.title: Congeners and darker liquors
segments.summary: Darker alcohols contain more impurities and are said to cause heavier hangovers, with a study comparing bourbon and vodka and notes on other liquors.

segments.title: Acetaldehyde, glutathione and why women suffer more
segments.summary: The liver turns alcohol into acetaldehyde, which is more toxic than alcohol; acetaldehyde dehydrogenase and cysteine in glutathione neutralize it, but glutathione stores are limited, and women have less, leading to harsher hangovers.

segments.title: Beer before liquor, age 24 and vomiting
segments.summary: Carbonation in beer speeds alcohol absorption, and the hosts discuss the order-of-drinks rhyme and the observation that hangovers get worse around age 24. Vomiting is discussed as a way to relieve stomach irritation, with a warning against self-induced vomiting.

segments.title: Hangover cures: hair of the dog, coffee, food, banana, eggs
segments.summary: Hair of the dog is debunked, and coffee's caffeine may ease headache but it is diuretic. Fatty food may line the stomach, and bananas, eggs, and uncarbonated water with sugar and salt or fruit juice are suggested to restore balance.

segments.title: Aspirin, hangover pills and drinking pace
segments.summary: Aspirin as a prostaglandin inhibitor is discussed, with a warning about stomach upset. Over-the-counter hangover pills are described as mostly vitamins plus water. Drinking water between drinks and moderation are recommended, with personal anecdotes about gin and tequila.

segments.title: Kiva promotion
segments.summary: The hosts promote Kiva microloans and the Stuff You Should Know team page, and point to further reading on hangovers on HowStuffWorks.

segments.title: Listener mail: former census enumerator
segments.summary: Mark, a former 2000 Census enumerator from Fishkill, New York, describes door-to-door visits, hostile residents, and a dog incident, and suggests a future topic.
